quickAnswer: Weston has the highest median home value of the 50 towns we serve, $1,434,000, and the 5th-oldest median build year, 1962. Utility gas heats 64.5% of homes, 6th highest, so equipment choices here are long-term decisions about older, valuable houses.
body: ## Number one for home value, and an old housing stock

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) puts the median value of an owner-occupied Weston home at $1,434,000. That is the highest of the 50 towns we serve, and more than double the $579,150 of the middle town. The median year built is 1962, fifth from the oldest, against 1975 for the middle town.

Of 3,967 housing units, 2,703 were built before 1980, or 68.1%, the 9th-highest share. Units dated 1939 or earlier number 934 (23.5%), the 8th-highest share, followed by 957 from 1940 to 1959 (24.1%) and 812 from 1960 to 1979 (20.5%). Newer housing exists too: 681 units (17.2%) date from 2000 or later, and 305 (7.7%) from 2010 on.

So Weston houses are valuable and, in most cases, old enough that the original heating and insulation choices belong to another era. A replacement here is rarely a quick like-for-like swap, and we assess the home's heating load before quoting a system so the equipment fits the house as it is now.
## Gas dominates, oil trails

Of 3,741 occupied homes, 2,412 use utility gas, 64.5% and 6th highest of 50, compared with 41.9% for the middle town. Fuel oil or kerosene heats 874 homes (23.4%, 40th), electricity 337 (9.0%) and bottled or tank gas 99 (2.6%).

For the 874 homes on oil, the decision at replacement is wider than for gas households. A gas main may or may not run to the property, and only the gas company can say. Weston ranks 40th for oil share, so oil is a smaller part of the picture than in most towns.
## Detached houses on large, preserved land

Single-family detached houses account for 3,384 units (85.3%), 9th among the 50 towns, and owners occupy 3,251 households (86.9%). Renters number 490 (13.1%). Buildings of two or more units hold 416 units (10.5%), the 39th-highest share.

Weston is a predominantly residential community where detached houses dominate, with a population density among the lowest of Boston's suburbs near or within Route 128. More than 2,000 acres, 18 percent of the town, are preserved as parks, fields, wetlands and forests. Vacancy is 5.7% (226 units), 9th highest and above the 3.6% of the middle town.
## Taverns, estates and postwar subdivision

Weston began as part of the Watertown settlement of 1630, set off as The Farms in 1698 and incorporated as a town in 1713. By the 18th century residents served travelers on the Boston Post Road, where the Josiah Smith Tavern and the Golden Ball Tavern still stand. The Worcester Turnpike opened in 1810 and the Boston and Worcester Railroad came through in 1834.

Country estates began to appear in the 1860s and were widespread by 1900. After World War II, Routes 128 and the Massachusetts Turnpike and pent-up demand led to the subdivision of estates and farms. More than half of the housing stock was built between 1950 and 1979, and in recent years many of those postwar houses have been replaced by much larger houses.
## Rebates depend on the utility
Heat pump rebates run through the electric utility that serves an address, so confirm yours first, then read the [heat pump page](/cities/weston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Does Weston's high home value affect how I should choose a heating system?
faq.a: It raises the stakes. At $1,434,000 the median value is the highest of 50 towns, so the house is a large asset and equipment is chosen for the long run. Ask for written estimates that compare a like-for-like unit with a heat pump or a conversion, and look at sizing before price.

faq.q: Is natural gas available at my Weston address?
faq.a: Utility gas heats 2,412 Weston homes, but availability is street by street. The gas company can tell you whether a main runs past your property and what a connection would involve. If you now burn oil, that answer decides whether a conversion belongs in the comparison.

faq.q: My Weston house was torn down and rebuilt larger. Does the system need to be bigger?
faq.a: Not automatically, but the load is likely different. Larger houses can mean more floor area, more windows and more zones, and a modern envelope may be tighter than before. The right size comes from a load calculation of the new building, not from the equipment in the house that stood there.

faq.q: Which heat pump rebate applies to a Weston home?
faq.a: It depends on the electric utility serving the address, so confirm that first. The program, the weatherization condition and the installer requirement all follow from it, and terms can change. Check masssave.com or ask the utility, then have the written estimate show the size and the number of zones.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Weston has 2,412 homes on utility gas, 874 on oil or kerosene and 99 on bottled gas. Replacement means matching the new system to a valuable, often older house, with a permit for gas work.
body: ## What the fuel mix means at replacement
In the ACS 2022, 2,412 Weston homes use utility gas, 874 use fuel oil or kerosene, 337 use electricity and 99 use bottled or tank gas. A failed boiler leads to a different conversation in each group.

Gas households mostly decide on size, venting and efficiency of the new appliance. Oil households may stay with oil, convert if a main is available, or consider a heat pump for part or all of the load. Bottled gas households have a delivered fuel and a tank to consider. Electric households can ask whether a heat pump would cut their power use for the same warmth.
### Permit rules for gas work

Gas permits in Massachusetts can only be pulled by licensed plumbers and gas fitters. A new gas furnace or boiler normally needs a permit and a final inspection, and the building department can explain how Weston handles it.
### Larger replacement houses

The town history notes that many postwar houses have been replaced by much larger ones. A large new house may have several zones and a higher heating load than the one it replaced, so equipment sized for a smaller predecessor will not do. Load is calculated for the building as it stands.
### Older houses

With 934 units dated 1939 or earlier and 957 from 1940 to 1959, many Weston houses are old enough that piping, radiators and chimneys are not original to a modern system. Swapping a boiler may also mean looking at flues and distribution.
### Rentals

Weston has 490 renter households, 13.1% of the total and 34th of 50. In the heating season a rental unit must be kept at 68 F by day and 64 F overnight (105 CMR 410.201), and the landlord pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise. This is not legal advice.
### Emergency calls
If the heat fails on a cold night, call (508) 786-8755, because emergency calls are taken 24 hours a day. A written estimate is free and comes before work starts.

faq.q: Should I replace my Weston oil boiler with gas?
faq.a: Only if gas is available and the numbers work. Oil heats 874 Weston homes (23.4%), and gas heats 2,412. A conversion depends on the connection to the main and the cost of a new gas unit. Compare it with a new oil boiler and a heat pump in writing before choosing.

faq.q: My historic Weston house has radiators and no ducts. What are my options?
faq.a: You can keep a boiler and radiators with a new boiler, or add ductless heat pump heads that need no ducts. The best choice depends on the rooms, the work allowed on the building and the load. A site visit shows what is practical without altering the character of the house.

faq.q: How do I know whether to repair or replace?
faq.a: Compare the failed part, the age of the unit and the cost of the repair with the cost of a new system. A small repair on a younger unit usually makes sense, while a cracked heat exchanger or repeated failures usually point to replacement. Ask for both figures in writing.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Weston has 3,384 detached houses, 161 townhouses and 416 units in multi-unit buildings. Cooling a large detached house often means zones, so ductless heads and ducted systems both come up.
body: ## Cooling a town of detached houses

The ACS 2022 counts 3,384 single-family detached houses among Weston's 3,967 units, along with 161 attached townhouses, 76 units in two-unit buildings, 107 in buildings of three or four and 233 in buildings of five or more. Detached houses are 85.3% of the stock, 9th among the 50 towns.
### Large houses, several zones

A large house rarely cools evenly from one thermostat. Upper floors, rooms with big windows and additions can behave like separate climates. Cooling by zone, with either multiple ducted air handlers or ductless heads, can match each area to its own load.
### Older houses without ducts

With 934 units from 1939 or earlier and 957 from 1940 to 1959, a share of Weston houses were designed before central air. Those with hot-water heat usually have no ducts to share, which makes ductless heads or high-velocity small-duct systems options worth pricing. Where space allows, a ducted system can also be added.
### Newer houses

Weston counts 681 units from 2000 or later, and 305 from 2010. A newer house may already have ducts sized for cooling, though that varies. The check is whether the existing system matches the present load.

- Which wings or floors run hot, and at what hour.
- Outdoor unit locations that keep sound and sight lines in check on a large lot.
- Spare capacity in the electrical service.
- Whether a heat pump could pick up part of the heating load as well.
### Lots and building types

Houses on large lots usually have the yard space for condensers, while townhouses and apartments are tighter. At 5.9% of units, buildings of five or more are a small part of Weston's stock, so most cooling projects here are single-owner decisions about a detached house.
### Sizing and moisture
A cooling system that is too big shuts off before it has dried the air. A measured load per zone avoids that problem and tends to give steadier comfort.
### Heat pump tie-in
Weston's 337 electric-heat homes can pair cooling with heat in one system, and the [heat pump page](/cities/weston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers that route.

faq.q: How do I cool the upstairs of a big Weston house?
faq.a: Often with a dedicated zone for the upper floor, either a small air handler or ductless heads. A single system pushing cool air upward rarely satisfies both floors. The right design follows the floor plan, where ducts can run and where the outdoor unit may sit.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a hot-water heated house?
faq.a: Yes. Ductless mini-splits need no ducts, only a small opening for each line set, so they suit radiator-heated houses. Where an attic or closet has room, a small-duct system is a third route. A site visit decides which fits.

faq.q: What should I check before summer?
faq.a: Run the system early to see that it cools, clear leaves and debris from the outdoor unit and replace the filter. If the unit is weak or noisy, a spring service visit can find a cause before a hot week arrives. That also gives time to plan if the equipment is near the end.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Weston has 874 oil or kerosene homes, 99 on bottled gas and 337 on electricity, plus 2,412 on gas. The utility serving the address decides the rebate path, and only 681 units date from 2000 or later.
body: ## Heat pumps in the highest-value town

A 2026 Mass Save rebate for a whole-home heat pump pays $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500, after the house has been weatherized. Everything else about eligibility is on the [heat pump services page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Which fuel groups compare

Oil heats 874 Weston homes and bottled gas heats 99. A heat pump replaces some of that delivered fuel, so those are the natural comparisons. Weston's 337 electric-heat households can ask if a heat pump would give the same warmth for less electricity. And the 2,412 gas homes may value a heat pump most for cooling and mild-weather heating, since gas still serves them well in deep winter.
### Weatherization and the age of the stock

Only 681 Weston units date from 2000 or later, and they pass the weatherization condition by date. Older units would typically start with a Home Energy Assessment, and with 68.1% of the stock built before 1980, what that assessment recommends could differ widely from house to house.
### Historic and older houses

Weston has one Local Historic District, 10 National Register Districts, 26 Historic Areas and seven houses individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places. If a house sits in one of these, ask what is permitted for outdoor equipment before ordering. Ductless systems are often chosen for such houses because they need no ducts, but exterior placement still matters.
### Ducted, ductless or hybrid

Ducted units can use existing ducts when they are sound. Ductless heads serve radiator-heated rooms and additions. A hybrid keeps the boiler for the coldest days, which suits owners who want a backup in a large house.
### Sizing

Sizing follows from the load calculation, which is done before we quote. The proposal should show capacity at low outdoor temperatures. See the [cooling page](/cities/weston/air-conditioning-installation-repair) for summer.

faq.q: Is a heat pump realistic for a large Weston house?
faq.a: Yes, often with several zones. A large house may need multiple indoor units or ducted air handlers, and the load calculation shows how many. The cost and complexity grow with size, so compare a hybrid, where the existing boiler stays for the coldest days, with a full replacement.

faq.q: My Weston house is in a historic district. Can I install outdoor equipment?
faq.a: Ask the town before you order. Historic districts can have rules on exterior changes, and the Weston Historical Commission is the body that protects the town's historic resources. A ductless system helps by avoiding ducts, but the location of the condenser is where review is likeliest.

faq.q: Does a heat pump work if I already have gas heat?
faq.a: It can. Many owners add a heat pump for cooling and for mild-weather heating, and keep the gas boiler or furnace for the coldest days. Whether it saves money depends on fuel and electricity prices and on the sizing, so ask the proposal to show how the two systems share the load.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Weston has 3,251 owner-occupied households and 874 oil or kerosene homes. Each fuel has its own routine, and a house that stands empty needs extra care before the weather turns.
body: ## Maintenance for valuable houses

Owners hold 3,251 Weston households (86.9%), and the median home is worth $1,434,000. A heating or cooling failure in a house of that value can mean damage beyond the equipment, from frozen pipes to wet ceilings, so maintenance is cheap protection.
### What each system needs

For the 874 oil homes the yearly job is a full burner cleaning, a new nozzle and filter, and a combustion reading. The 2,412 gas homes need a safety check of the burner, venting and controls. Heat pumps need clean coils, fresh filters and clear drains. Bottled gas homes, 99 in town, add the tank and regulator to the inspection.
### Vacant and seasonal homes

Weston has 226 vacant housing units, a 5.7% vacancy rate that ranks 9th of 50. A house that sits empty still needs its heat ready for winter and its drains clear in summer. A fall check and a plan for someone to look in during cold weather are good insurance.
### Older and larger systems

Large houses often have more than one boiler, furnace or air handler, and each needs its own service. Older equipment in houses from 1939 or earlier, of which Weston has 934, may need parts that are no longer easy to find. A tune-up is the time to ask about the remaining life.

- **Fall:** heating tune-up for every unit, filters changed.
- **Spring:** cooling check, condensate drains tested, outdoor units cleared.
- **Any time:** unusual smells, soot or an alarm sounding means stop using the unit and call.
### Why a log helps

With several systems in one large house, a simple list of what was serviced and when keeps visits on schedule. It also shows patterns, such as a zone that keeps losing pressure, that a single visit might miss.
### Between visits

Change filters on schedule, keep snow off outdoor units and look at thermostat batteries and settings before calling. A note of fuel, rough age and nameplate data speeds up any phone call. If the visit finds equipment past saving, see the [heating page](/cities/weston/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a Weston oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, ahead of the heating season. The visit cleans the burner, replaces the nozzle and filter and checks combustion. With 874 oil or kerosene homes in town, it is a routine chore for many owners, and skipping it risks soot buildup and a breakdown during a cold week.

faq.q: Should I service equipment in a house we use only part of the year?
faq.a: Yes. Systems that sit idle can fail when they are needed, and an unnoticed problem in an empty house can become damage. Test heating before cold weather and cooling before summer, and arrange for someone to check the house during extreme weather.

faq.q: Do multiple zones need separate service visits?
faq.a: Each piece of equipment needs its own check, but they can usually be done in one appointment. Tell us how many boilers, furnaces, air handlers and outdoor units you have so the visit is planned properly. The nameplate details for each help the technician arrive prepared.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Weston's housing spans 934 units dated 1939 or earlier to 681 dated 2000 or later. More than 2,000 acres of the town are preserved as parks, fields, wetlands and forests, so outdoor moisture and pollen are part of the picture.
body: ## Air in old and new Weston houses

The ACS 2022 divides Weston's 3,967 housing units into 934 from 1939 or earlier, 957 from 1940 to 1959, 812 from 1960 to 1979, 583 from 1980 to 1999 and 681 from 2000 or later. Each era moves air differently.
### The oldest houses

Houses from 1939 or earlier tend to leak around windows, sills and chimneys. Old materials in them may need testing by a qualified specialist before a renovation disturbs them. Ductwork in these houses, if present, may have been collecting dust for decades.
### Tighter new construction

The town's history notes that many postwar houses are being replaced by much larger ones. New houses can be very tight, and large tight houses need planned ventilation so that moisture and cooking fumes do not build up. Bath fans, range hoods and a fresh-air supply are the basics.
### Wetlands, forests and drained ground

The town covers 17.3 square miles, 1.85% of it water, and more than 2,000 acres (18 percent) are preserved as parks, fields, wetlands and forests. Houses near wetlands or woods can meet damp basements, pollen and mold spores. In 1913 the Town Green was made by draining and landscaping an existing wetland, which shows how long water has been a design question here.
### Humidity through the seasons
Winter heat dries the air, and summer humidity returns. Dehumidify damp basements after fixing the leak, and humidify only as much as keeps windows clear.
### Why the lot and the age both matter

A large house on a wooded lot and a compact house near the center may share a street, yet differ in how they take in air, moisture and pollen. That is why a walk through the actual building tells us more than the year of construction alone, and why we look at the basement, attic and equipment before suggesting anything.
### Options

- Filtration matched to your system's airflow.
- Dehumidification once water sources are fixed.
- Ventilation for tight houses.
- Duct cleaning when ducts show dirt, mold or damage.
Tests are snapshots; fixing the source is what lasts. For heating questions, see the [heating page](/cities/weston/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: Does a big new house in Weston need mechanical ventilation?
faq.a: Often it benefits from it. Tight houses trap moisture and fumes unless fresh air comes in. A ventilator or well-planned exhaust can address that. A humidity reading in winter and summer shows how the house is behaving, and a specialist can recommend a layout for the building.

faq.q: Is a musty basement in an older Weston house a health concern?
faq.a: Possibly, because damp materials and mold can send spores and odor upstairs. Start by finding where the water enters, whether through a crack, poor grading or condensation. A dehumidifier lowers humidity but cannot seal a wall. Persistent smell or visible growth calls for a specialist.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Only when there is something to see: dust deposits, mold, or damage from pests or building work. An inspection of the system comes first. Ducts that are cleaned without fixing the reason they got dirty, such as a leaky return, will collect dust again.
